numerical_failure.affected_api: pandas._libs.tslibs.timestamps._Timestamp.__add__ and pandas._libs.tslibs.timestamps._Timestamp.__sub__ (tz-naive timedelta64 ndarray branch, routed through _addsub_timedelta64_array)
numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For a tz-naive Timestamp plus or minus a timedelta64 ndarray, the raw self.asm8 +/- other wraps silently: once when numpy promotes both operands to the finer unit, and again in the addition itself, returning a wrong datetime64 array with no error.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The operation should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime (the same exception the tz-aware branch of the same method gives), and OutOfBoundsTimedelta when it is the coarser operand that has to be cast.
trigger_conditions: Operand is a timedelta64 ndarray (dtype kind 'm')
Timestamp unit and timedelta unit differ, so numpy promotes to the finer unit
Result overflows int64 when promoted to the finer unit or during the addition

numerical_characteristics.dtype: m8[ns] and m8[s] (timedelta64 ndarrays); Timestamp at unit 's' or 'ns'; big-endian '>m8[s]' buffer mentioned
numerical_characteristics.precision: Timestamp resolutions 4 (s, ms, us, ns); timedelta64 units 8 when verified; sub-nanosecond units (ps) fall through to numpy
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: Wraparound example: 2500-01-01 cast to ns overflows; 2**62 seconds as m8[s] overflows timedelta64; a big-endian read produced year 2283416254; verification over 400 magnitudes
category_specific_evidence: Property violated: numpy promotes to the finer unit and wraps on the cast and on the addition, so Timestamp +/- timedelta64 ndarray silently wraps instead of raising; the fix routes the tz-naive path through add_overflowsafe so it raises OutOfBoundsDatetime like the tz-aware path.
Concrete value: Timestamp('2500-01-01').as_unit('s') + np.array([1], dtype='m8[ns]') must raise OutOfBoundsDatetime with message 'Cannot cast 2500-01-01 00:00:00 to unit=ns without overflow'.
Concrete value: Timestamp('2000-01-01').as_unit('ns') + np.array([2**62], dtype='m8[s]') must raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta with message 'Cannot convert 4611686018427387904 seconds to timedelta64'.
Adjacent bug: ts.as_unit('s') + np.array([1], '>m8[s]') returned 2283416254 years due to int64 view misreading non-native byteorder.
Verification: exact Python-int oracle across 4 Timestamp resolutions x 8 timedelta64 units x 400 magnitudes x add/sub gave 0 mismatches, 0 spurious raises, 0 missed raises.
NaT propagation: ts(2000-01-01 s) + [NaT, 1s] yields ['NaT','2000-01-01 00:00:01'] and subtraction yields ['NaT','1999-12-31 23:59:59'].

Preserved numpy behaviour: m8[Y]/m8[M] and sub-ns units fall through to numpy (astype_overflowsafe would convert a year as 365 days and truncate 1 ps to 0 us); generic m8 read in the other operand's unit; 0-dim input returns numpy scalar.
Performance cost: 1M-element Timestamp + m8[us] went 1.3 ms to 14.9 ms.
reproduction_risks: Year/month and sub-nanosecond units are intentionally left to numpy, so they do not raise and should not be expected to match the new behaviour.
Big-endian m8 arrays were a separate adjacent bug; reproduction on native-byteorder data may not exercise it.
Per-element add_overflowsafe cost makes large-array timings much slower than before.

provenance.value: pandas._libs.tslibs.timestamps._Timestamp.__add__ and pandas._libs.tslibs.timestamps._Timestamp.__sub__ (tz-naive timedelta64 ndarray branch, routed through _addsub_timedelta64_array)

For a tz-naive Timestamp plus or minus a timedelta64 ndarray, the raw self.asm8 +/- other wraps silently: once when numpy promotes both operands to the finer unit, and again in the addition itself, returning a wrong datetime64 array with no error.
